'''John P. Abraham''' is a professor of mechanical engineering and thermal sciences in the College of Engineering at the [[University of St. Thomas (Minnesota)|University of St. Thomas]] in [[Minnesota]], United States. He teaches and carries out research in mechanical engineering in the thermal sciences, biomedical engineering, renewable energy, medical devices, burn injuries, electronics and datacenter cooling, climate change and with other engineered devices. 

He cam to public prominence in 2009 after analyzing misrepresentations being used to promote [[climate change denial]], and from 2010 became a prominent defender of science in the [[global warming controversy]]. In that year, he helped to launch the [[Climate Science Rapid Response Team]].

==Career==
Abraham is professor of thermal science ([[thermodynamics]]) and [[fluid mechanics]] at the [[University of St. Thomas (Minnesota)|University of St. Thomas School of Engineering]], [[Minnesota]].<ref name=ustbio>[http://www.stthomas.edu/engineering/faculty/jpabraham.htm University of St. Thomas : School of Engineering : John P. Abraham, Ph.D] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100527172313/http://www.stthomas.edu/engineering/faculty/jpabraham.htm |date=May 27, 2010 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.stthomas.edu/engineering/ University of St. Thomas : School of Engineering] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110108183708/http://www.stthomas.edu/engineering/ |date=January 8, 2011 }}</ref> His area of research includes thermodynamics, [[heat transfer]], [[fluid flow]], [[numerical simulation]], and [[energy]]. After gaining his doctorate at the [[University of Minnesota]] in 2002, he joined St. Thomas as an adjunct instructor, later becoming a full-time member of the faculty. He has published over 600 papers in journals, conferences, book chapters, books, and patents. Since 1997 has also been an engineering consultant working on industrial research in aerospace, biomedical, energy and manufacturing industries. He has also served as an expert witness in numerous scald and injury lawsuits and for intellectual property (patent) cases and in other litigations. He works on clean and renewable wind and solar projects in the developing world, and has also produced numerous books, such as a 2014 text on small-scale wind power<ref>{{Cite book |last=Abraham |first=J. P. |title=Small-scale wind power : design, analysis, and environmental impacts |date=2014 |publisher=McGraw-Hill Education |others=Brian Plourde |isbn=978-1-60650-485-7 |location=New York |oclc=1100883111}}</ref> and a 2010 groundbreaking text on laminar-to-turbulent fluid flow.<ref>[http://courseweb.stthomas.edu/jpabraham/ John P. Abraham, University of St. Thomas, MN] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100608132508/http://courseweb.stthomas.edu/jpabraham/ |date=June 8, 2010 }}</ref><ref name="STM Winter12">{{Cite web | last = Winterer | first = Jim | title = John Abraham Takes a Stand | url = http://www.stthomas.edu/news/2012/02/28/3615/ | publisher = St. Thomas Magazine | date = Winter 2012 | accessdate = 20 March 2012 | archive-date = 22 February 2014 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140222185649/http://www.stthomas.edu/news/2012/02/28/3615/ | url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Abraham |first=J P |title=Modeling Internal Flows by an Extended Menter Transition Model |url=https://www.novapublishers.com/catalog/product_info.php?products_id=32244&osCsid=fe6438e821a248cdd0b8479b10443247 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141103064004/https://www.novapublishers.com/catalog/product_info.php?products_id=32244&osCsid=fe6438e821a248cdd0b8479b10443247 |archive-date=2014-11-03 |access-date=2014-11-03}}</ref>

== Research ==
Abraham has been cited over 16,000 times<ref>{{Cite web |title=Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Wbjde1sAAAAJ |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> by his peers in the scientific community and he has 16 articles with Altmetric scores above the top 5%. His active research includes ocean warming that has received extensive press attention<ref>{{Cite web |last=Huttner |first=Paul |last2=Alvarez |first2=Matt |date=2025-09-19 |title=Changes in Atlantic Ocean current may be sign of climate tipping point, scientist says |url=https://www.mprnews.org/episode/2025/09/19/changes-in-atlantic-ocean-current-may-be-sign-of-climate-tipping-point-scientist-says |access-date=2026-09-11 |website=MPR News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.pbs.org/video/tipping-point-1710885723/ |title=PBS News Hour {{!}} Climate researcher on record rise in ocean temperatures {{!}} Season 2024 |language=en |access-date=2026-09-11 |via=www.pbs.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-13 |title=Ocean heat shatters record with warming equal to 5 atomic bombs exploding "every second" for a year. ==Refutation of climate change denial==
Abraham felt it was necessary to respond to a talk given to the [[David Strom|Minnesota Free Market Institute]] in October 2009 by a well-known [[climate change denial|denier of human-caused]] [[global warming]],<ref>[[Michael E. Mann]]: ''The Hockey-Stick and the Climate Wars''. Columbia University Press, 2012, p. 71.</ref> [[Christopher Monckton, 3rd Viscount Monckton of Brenchley|Christopher Monckton]]. He thought "this guy is a great speaker and he is very convincing. If I didn't know the science, I would believe him. Frankly, the nonscientists in the audience didn't have a chance. They had no way of knowing what he said was not true. I felt Monckton took advantage of them and he knew he was taking advantage of them." In the following months he carried out research, contacting scientists cited by Monckton, and in late May 2010, he posted online an 83-minute video rebutting Monckton's statements. This attracted little attention at first, until it was highlighted by an article [[George Monbiot]] published in ''[[The Guardian]]''.<ref name="STM Winter12" /><ref>[http://www.stthomas.edu/engineering/jpabraham/ Abraham presentation] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100804204514/http://www.stthomas.edu/engineering/jpabraham/ |date=August 4, 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/blog/2010/jun/03/monckton-us-climate-change-talk-denial |location=London |work=The Guardian |first=John |last=Abraham |title=Monckton takes scientist to brink of madness at climate change talk |date=3 June 2010 |archiveurl=https://www.webcitation.org/5rDKTWCrT?url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/environment/blog/2010/jun/03/monckton-us-climate-change-talk-denial |archivedate=14 July 2010 |url-status=live }}<br />{{citation|title=Viscount Monckton, another fallen idol of climate denial/Professor John Abraham's withering scrutiny reveals how the gurus of climate scepticism repeat a pattern of manipulation |date=3 June 2010 |author=George Monbiot |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/georgemonbiot/2010/jun/03/monckton-climate-change |location=London |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://www.webcitation.org/5qDn1CUO9?url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/environment/georgemonbiot/2010/jun/03/monckton-climate-change |archive-date= 3 June 2010 }}</ref>

In November 2010, Abraham (and two colleagues, [[Scott Mandia]] and [[Ray Weymann]]) launched the [[Climate Science Rapid Response Team]], to provide rapid, high-quality scientific information to the media and government decision-makers. The intention of this group is to enable scientists to share their work directly with the general public. This effort has been covered by many media outlets.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2010-nov-08-la-na-climate-scientists-20101108-story.html |work=Los Angeles Times Abraham estimated early in 2012 that since beginning his rebuttal he had put around 1,000 unpaid hours into work on climate change and the controversy. He has given numerous speeches to publicize global warming issues, but does not accept funding for climate research or ask for an honorarium for speeches: if payment is given he asks that it goes to St. Thomas or to charity.<ref name="STM Winter12" />
